author: New China TV
description:
What can a 5,000 USD donation nurture over 26 years? For Ronald Sakolsky, a retired American teacher who once taught in Luoyang, a city in central China, the answer is a vast green rising from Maowusu Sandy Land, located in Ordos of north China's Inner Mongolia.
In 1999, Sakolsky learned about Yin Yuzhen and her relentless efforts in fighting desertification through tree planting at Maowusu. Inspired by her commitment, he raised and donated 5,000 US dollars to support her afforestation work. In the second year, his colleague Bai Fan, now general principal of Luoyang No.2 Foreign Language School Education Group, accompanied Sakolsky to Maowusu, where they met Yin in person. Their shared dream of turning sand into green began to take root.
In the years that followed, Yin transformed Sakolsky's donation into a thriving forest. This year, she reconnected with him and invited him back to the sandy land to see how it had changed. On August 24, outside Yin's home, Sakolsky and Bai reunited a
title: Old friends reunite after 26 years in a sandy land forest their kindness helped grow

author: New China TV
description:
In 2000, American teacher Ronald Sakolsky traveled to the Maowusu Sandy Land in Ordos, Inner Mongolia, to visit Yin Yuzhen, to whom he had donated 5,000 USD a year ago in support of her tree-planting and desertification-control work.
Little could he have imagined that through Yin's tireless efforts, his act of kindness from across the ocean would one day grow into a forest.
With the help of the media, Yin finally reconnected with Sakolsky this May and invited him back to the sandy land to see for himself changes that had taken place over the past 27 years.
At 5:45 p.m. on August 23, Sakolsky arrived in Ordos aboard Air China Flight CA1149. Yin, accompanied by her husband and younger son, was there to welcome him.
Returning to Ordos after more than two decades, how did Sakolsky feel about the long-awaited reunion and the extraordinary transformation he was about to witness?
title: After 26 years apart, Chinese desertification-control hero reunites with American friend in Ordos
